title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.15-17): k is a principal ideal domain. L_· is a '∂-ps. ch.' object, a (half-)simplicial k-module with suitable finiteness and projectivity conditions. L^! is its associated normalized chain complex, so π_i(L_·) = H_i(L^!). The previous page states a structure theorem. L_· is isomorphic to a product of three kinds of factor. (a) μ_i copies of an elementary contractible model Λ^iΦ, whose chain complex is k --id--> k in degrees i, i-1. (b) ν_j copies of Λ^jΨ, an Eilenberg–MacLane-type model whose chain complex is k[j]. (c) ρ_{i,ℓ} copies of Φ(i,ℓ), whose chain complex is k --ℓ--> k in degrees i, i-1. Here ℓ ranges over P = N^(Max k) − {0}, the nonzero effective divisors of k other than units.

This page gives the uniqueness half. The multiplicities are determined by invariants of L^!:
(a) For each i ≥ 1, the ℓ with ρ_{i,ℓ} ≠ 0 are the elementary divisors of the torsion of π_{i-1}(L) = H_{i-1}(L^!), and ρ_{i,ℓ} is the multiplicity of ℓ.
(b) ν_i = rank π_i(L) = rank H_i(L^!).
(c) μ_i = rank B_{i-1}(L^!) − ρ_i, where ρ_i = Σ_ℓ ρ_{i,ℓ}.
(d) As consistency relations: rank Z_i = μ_{i+1} + ρ_{i+1} + ν_i, and rank L^!_i = μ_{i+1} + μ_i + ρ_{i+1} + ρ_i + ν_i.
The sentence after this is only partly legible. It apparently says that L_· is determined up to isomorphism by these numerical functions.

Proof sketch:
- Dold–Puppe (Dold–Kan) reduces everything to chain complexes of finitely generated projectives.
- Over a PID, submodules of finitely generated free modules are free. So each B_{i-1} is projective, d: L^!_i → B_{i-1} splits, and the complex is a direct sum of two-term complexes K_i: P_i = B_{i-1} ↪ Q_i ≅ Z_{i-1}, sitting in degrees i, i-1.
- The next page splits Q_i further: the saturation P̄_i of P_i plus a free complement N_{i-1} ≅ H_{i-1}/tors, giving a piece N_{i-1}[i-1].
- Smith normal form then splits P_i ⊂ P̄_i into pieces k --n_α--> k. This yields the (c)-type factors, and the (a)-type factors when n_α is a unit.

The purpose is to describe completely the 'dévissage' of ∂-perfect half-simplicial modules over a PID, as preparation for studying multiplicative structures on them.
errors: Item (a) is loosely worded. The ρ_{i,ℓ} are not themselves the elementary divisors. Rather, the ℓ with ρ_{i,ℓ} ≠ 0 are the non-unit elementary divisors of tors π_{i-1}, and ρ_{i,ℓ} counts their multiplicity. The marginal insertion 'multiplicités' shows Grothendieck meant this.
The rank formulas (c) and (d) are correct. They follow from B_{i-1} having rank μ_i + ρ_i in the decomposition.
The decomposition is unique only up to non-unique isomorphism, as Grothendieck himself notes ('à isom. près, non unique'). Only the multiplicities are invariants.
No mathematical error otherwise. The argument is the standard splitting of complexes of free modules over a PID combined with Smith normal form.

ideas.what: Reduction of simplicial k-modules to chain complexes via the normalized complex
ideas.where_published: Used in Pursuing Stacks and in Illusie's work on the cotangent complex; Grothendieck refers to Dold–Puppe in several places

ideas.what: Any complex of finitely generated free modules over a PID splits as a sum of two-term complexes k --n--> k and shifted copies of k, with multiplicities fixed by the homology ranks, the torsion elementary divisors and the boundary ranks
ideas.modern_name: Classification of perfect complexes over a PID (Smith normal form); minimal decomposition of free chain complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Smith normal form; e.g. used in Moore's and in Whitehead's work on chain complexes)

ideas.what: Corresponding decomposition of simplicial (or half-simplicial) modules into elementary simplicial models: contractible pieces Λ^iΦ, Eilenberg–MacLane pieces Λ^jΨ, and Moore-type pieces Φ(i,ℓ) indexed by effective divisors
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of simplicial abelian groups into products of Eilenberg–MacLane and Moore-type simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.C. Moore (simplicial abelian groups are products of K(π,n)); Dold

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully but routinely applies Dold–Kan and Smith normal form to classify perfect simplicial modules over a PID. The only individual touch is the notation: the elementary models Λ^iΦ, Λ^jΨ and Φ(i,ℓ) indexed by effective divisors, which point toward the later 'multiplicative structures' theme. The mathematics itself is standard.
transcription_corrections: The final display should read: P_i = B_{i-1} ⊂ Z_{i-1} ≅ Q_i. In the image, '=' (drawn vertically) links P_i to B_{i-1} and '≀' links Q_i to Z_{i-1}.
In (a) the marginal insertion 'multiplicités' sits above 'diviseurs élémentaires'. The intended reading is 'les ρ_{i,ℓ} ≠ 0 sont les multiplicités des diviseurs élémentaires de π_{i-1}(L_·)'.
'Dém [-La forme-] {+Dém+} la théorie de Dold-Puppe' should more likely read 'Dém. Par la théorie de Dold-Puppe'.

The line after (d) is only partly legible. It seems to say that L_· is determined up to isomorphism by the numerical functions (multiplicities) involved. The '[?]' guesses in the machine transcription are uncertain.
The struck word before 'à comp. proj. de t.f.' may be 'borné'. The inserted word is uncertain and not clearly 'différentiel'.
The insertion '{+unique+}' near 'à isom.' is more likely 'non uniques', contrasted with '(mais libres)'.
